name: Go Fish
description: Go Fish is a classic set-collection game where players ask opponents for ranks they already hold, then draw from stock on failure, aiming to complete the most four-of-a-kind books.

overview.description: Go Fish is a classic set-collection game where players ask opponents for ranks they already hold, then draw from stock on failure, aiming to complete the most four-of-a-kind books.

history.origins: Derived from 19th-century 'Happy Families' and 'Authors' games, which used special decks. The adaptation to standard playing cards occurred in the United States around the turn of the 20th century.
timeline: 1851: 'Authors' published in the USA, introducing the mechanic of asking for specific cards to complete sets.
1861: 'Happy Families' published in the UK with similar rules.
20th Century: 'Go Fish' becomes the standard name for the game when played with a regular 52-card deck.
Present: Remains a starter game for millions of children worldwide.
history.cultural: Used widely as an educational tool for teaching numbers, matching, and memory skills.
history.evolution: Special-pack family games such as Authors and Happy Families were adapted to standard ranks, producing modern Go Fish rules.

setup.dealing: Deal 7 cards each (for 2 players) or 5 cards each (for 3+ players). The rest form the 'Ocean' (Stock) spread out face-down.
setup.equipment: No equipment beyond deck; optional score sheet for multi-hand sessions.

rules.objective: Collect the highest number of books (four cards of one rank) by successful asks and stock draws.
rules.gameplay:
1. **The Ask**: On your turn, ask any player for a specific rank (e.g., 'Alice, do you have any 3s '). **Rule**: You must already hold at least one card of that rank.
2. **The Catch**: If they have the cards, they MUST give ALL of them to you. You get another turn.
3. **The Fish**: If they have none, they say 'Go Fish!'. You draw one card from the Stock. - **Lucky Catch**: If you draw the rank you asked for, show it to everyone and take another turn. - **Miss**: If you draw anything else, your turn ends.
4. **Books**: When you have 4 of a kind, reveal them and place them face-up in front of you.
5. **Empty Hand**: If you run out of cards, draw new ones from the stock (usually 1, sometimes 5 depending on house rules).
keyRules: You may ask only for a rank you currently hold at least one of.
A player who is asked must hand over all cards of that rank.
When an ask fails, draw one card; if it matches the requested rank, your turn continues.
As soon as a book is completed, it is laid down and removed from hand.

strategy.basic: Always ask for ranks you actually hold (it's the rules!). Start by asking for ranks where you already have 2 or 3 cards to finish books quickly.
strategy.intermediate: Listen! If Bob asks Alice for Kings, Bob has at least one King. If Alice says 'Go Fish', she has no Kings. Remember this.
strategy.advanced: The Steal: If Bob asks Alice for Kings and she gives him one, you *know* Bob has Kings. On your turn, if you have a King, ask Bob for his Kings to steal them all before he can complete the book.
tips: Don't sort your hand too obviously if playing with sharp-eyed opponents.
In a 2-player game, card counting is powerful. If you know your opponent doesn't have 7s (because they fished earlier), don't ask for them.

variations.name: Ask Specific Card
variations.description: Players ask for an exact card (for example seven of diamonds) instead of rank only.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation changes ask target only; no engine constants to override.

variations.name: Continue After Stock Empty
variations.description: After stock is exhausted, asking continues without drawing until all books are formed.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Rule change only; game end and draw behavior described in variation text.

variations.name: Refill Empty Hand
variations.description: When a player runs out of cards, they draw up to five cards from stock if available and continue play.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Refill amount is described in variation; no engine numeric overrides needed.

scoring.description: Players earn points by collecting books (sets of four cards of the same rank). The player with the most books at game end wins.
scoring.winCondition: The player with the most completed books (sets of 4 of the same rank) wins. In scoring variants, each book is worth 1 point.

synthesis.shortDescription: The quintessential family card game where players collect sets of four cards of the same rank by asking opponents for specific ranks. Combines set collection, memory, deduction, and social play in one of gaming's most accessible formats.

hero.title: GO FISH
hero.subtitle: The Classic Fishing Game
hero.tagline: Ask, collect, complete books. The simplest fun for all ages.
